site.name: meadowid
site.summary: MeadowID — identity dashboard (local demo) Fictional unified-identity dashboard. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Pages `index.html` — Overview Sidebar nav plus a four-tile stat row (Connected apps, Active sessions, Passkeys, Trust score), an "issues" alert list (unfamiliar session, weak factor, stale app), a recent sign-in ledger, and a recovery-readiness checklist. `connected-apps.html` — Connected apps Filterable / searchable list of every app that holds a token on the user's behalf. Each card shows scope chips (sensitive ones highlighted) and a Revoke button that requires confirmation. `devices.html` — Active sessions

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full meadowid system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: MeadowID presents a clean identity dashboard, but testing (covering 59% of interactive features) revealed several critical functional and responsive design gaps. On mobile, the main navigation overflows horizontally without affordances, hiding sections from users. Across the site, many critical actions (like removing passkeys or freezing the account) act as dead links or fail to provide visual feedback, and several form components lack accessibility labels or adequate touch targets.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and evaluate the MeadowID identity dashboard, focusing on navigation, security alerts, session/app management, and data export flows.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the Overview dashboard to validate alert dismissals and summary links. It will then proceed to manage connected apps and active sessions, testing filtering and revocation flows. Following that, authentication settings (passkeys, recovery, freezing) and data export will be examined. Finally, critical pages will be re-tested in a mobile viewport to assess the impact of identified small tap targets and table responsiveness.
assumptions: The application is a local frontend demo; actions like 'Revoke' or 'Add passkey' will likely trigger local UI state changes or mock dialogs rather than real backend requests.
Sidebar navigation links are present on all pages and serve as the primary routing mechanism.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets across the sidebar navigation (40px height).
Responsiveness of the 'Latest sign-ins' table and 'Connected apps' list on mobile viewports.
Clarity and confirmation steps for destructive actions (e.g., Revoke app, End all sessions, Freeze switch).

phases.title: Dashboard Overview & Alerts
phases.objective: Validate the primary dashboard widgets, alert interactions, and navigation entry points.
key_checks: Click 'Run security check' to see if it triggers an evaluation state.
Interact with 'Things to look at' items (e.g., click 'Review', 'Dismiss all').
Verify links in 'Latest sign-ins' and 'Recovery readiness' components navigate correctly.
exit_criteria: All alert actions and primary dashboard links have been clicked and their resulting states or navigations recorded.

phases.title: App & Session Management
phases.objective: Explore the connected apps and active sessions lists, focusing on filtering, sorting, and revocation.
key_checks: On connected-apps.html, test the search input and sort/category dropdowns.
Click 'Revoke' on an app and observe if a confirmation dialog appears.
On devices.html, interact with specific session rows and click 'End all other sessions'.
exit_criteria: Filtering/sorting controls are exercised and at least one revocation/end session flow is attempted.

phases.title: Authentication & Account Security
phases.objective: Evaluate the passkey management, backup factors, and account freeze functionalities.
key_checks: On passkeys.html, click '+ Add a passkey' and test 'Remove' / 'Reveal & download' actions.
Interact with the recovery email input and 'Send verification'.
On freeze.html, locate and toggle the freeze switch or perform the freeze action.
exit_criteria: Passkey addition/removal flows and account freeze interactions are documented.

phases.title: Data Export
phases.objective: Walk through the data export configuration flow.
key_checks: Toggle various data category checkboxes (e.g., Account profile, Sign-in history).
Click 'Continue' or 'Save as draft' to progress the export flow.
exit_criteria: Data export form inputs are manipulated and submission buttons are tested.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Assess usability on small screens, specifically focusing on navigation and complex layouts.
key_checks: Verify how the sidebar navigation adapts (e.g., hamburger menu).
Check horizontal scrolling or wrapping on the 'Latest sign-ins' table and 'Connected apps' list.
Re-evaluate the accessibility of the small tap targets identified in the prescan.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout adaptations are captured via screenshots and any overflow or tap target issues are logged.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 6 HTML pages listed in the prescan.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise filtering/sorting, simulated security/revocation actions, and form toggles across all pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate navigation menu, tables, and lists on index, connected apps, and devices pages.

notes: Since this is a static site with JavaScript, pay close attention to DOM mutations (modals, toasts, list filtering) that occur without page loads.

findings.user_goal: Navigate between dashboard sections on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The primary navigation menu does not collapse into a responsive mobile menu (e.g., a hamburger menu). Instead, it overflows horizontally off the screen with no visible scrollbar or fade effect to indicate more links exist.
findings.evidence: On mobile viewports: "The top navigation menu is not responsive; it fails to collapse... and instead overflows horizontally, forcing users to scroll horizontally to see all options (links extend to x=957px)."
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users may not realize there are other sections (like Passkeys or Data Export) and will struggle to access them if they don't accidentally swipe horizontally on the navbar.
findings.suggestion: Implement a collapsible hamburger menu for mobile breakpoints, or at least provide clear visual affordances (like a gradient fade or scrollbar) indicating horizontal scrollability.

findings.user_goal: Perform account management tasks like removing passkeys, revealing backup codes, dismissing alerts, or requesting deletion.
findings.problem: Numerous critical buttons and links are implemented as dead clicks (href="#") that do not trigger any state change, modal, or action when interacted with.
findings.evidence: Chunk summaries explicitly state: "The 'Dismiss all' button is non-functional... appends a '#' to the URL", "Clicking the 'Remove' button on a passkey produces no visible feedback", and "The 'Request deletion' link ... yields no feedback."
findings.why_it_matters: Users attempting critical security or privacy tasks will be completely blocked, leading to frustration and eroded trust in the platform's security controls.
findings.suggestion: Connect these actions to their respective functional logic, ensuring they open confirmation modals or perform the required state changes.

findings.user_goal: Find a specific connected app in a long list by category or name.
findings.problem: The 'Category' and 'Sort' dropdowns on the Connected apps page visually update when a new option is selected, but the underlying list of apps does not change or reorder.
findings.evidence: Observed that "Selecting 'Productivity' in the category filter... fails to filter the actual list of apps below it" and "the sort dropdown successfully visually updates to show 'Sort: Name A→Z', but the list ... fails to reorder."
findings.why_it_matters: Users with many connected apps will not be able to locate specific apps efficiently, rendering the provided sorting/filtering UI deceptive.
findings.suggestion: Bind the dropdown change events to the list rendering logic to actually filter and sort the DOM elements based on the selected values.

findings.user_goal: Secure a downloaded data export with a password.
findings.problem: Checking the 'Encrypt archive with a password' checkbox during the data export flow marks the checkbox as checked, but fails to reveal an input field to actually type the password.
findings.evidence: Agent observation: "Checking the 'Encrypt archive with a password (recommended)' checkbox successfully updates its visual state, but no password input field is revealed."
findings.why_it_matters: Users will be confused about how their archive will be encrypted if they were never prompted to provide a password, potentially blocking them from securely exporting data.
findings.suggestion: Add conditional logic that displays a password input field immediately below or next to the checkbox when it is toggled on.

findings.user_goal: Immediately lock down the account during a security incident.
findings.problem: The 'Freeze switch' on the Freeze account page is not detectable as a proper interactive element, preventing interaction.
findings.evidence: Trajectory notes: "The 'Freeze switch' toggle visible on the page is not detected as an interactive element. This suggests a critical accessibility or functional issue..."
findings.why_it_matters: If a user is under active attack and trying to freeze their account, a broken or inaccessible switch could lead to severe security compromises.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the toggle is built using a semantic <input type="checkbox"> or <button> with appropriate aria-pressed or aria-checked states, and ensure it visually registers clicks.

findings.user_goal: Execute background tasks like running a security check or saving an export draft.
findings.problem: Clicking 'Run security check' on the Overview page and 'Save as draft' on the Data Export page provides zero visual feedback (no loading spinners, toasts, or UI updates).
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunks note: "Clicking the 'Run security check' button provides no visual feedback" and "'Save as draft' button on the Export data page provides no visual feedback."
findings.why_it_matters: Without visual confirmation, users won't know if the system registered their click, potentially causing them to click multiple times or abandon the task assuming the site is broken.
findings.suggestion: Add a brief loading state to the buttons upon click, followed by a success toast or inline message confirming the action was completed or saved.
findings.source_hint: index.html ('Run security check') and data-export.html ('Save as draft')

findings.user_goal: Select formats, categories, and schedules for data export on a touch device.
findings.problem: Radio buttons and checkboxes throughout the Data Export wizard have tiny tap targets (e.g., 13x13px and 13x36px), falling far below mobile accessibility standards.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings generated: "The radio buttons for export formats (JSON, CSV, HTML) have tiny 13x13px tap targets" and "checkboxes have small tap targets (13x36px)".
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users will struggle to tap the correct options without accidentally selecting adjacent ones, increasing friction on touch interfaces.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the native inputs in <label> elements that encompass the text description, and apply padding to ensure the clickable area is at least 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Use screen readers to select options or enter an email address.
findings.problem: Several form inputs lack programmatic <label> elements or aria-label attributes linking them to their visible text headers.
findings.evidence: Observations note: "The 'Time range' <select> dropdown lacks a programmatically associated label", "email input field in Step 3 lacks a programmatic label", and "Connected apps page [filters] lack explicit text labels or ARIA labels."
findings.why_it_matters: Visually impaired users relying on assistive technology will hear these inputs announced as blank or generic fields, preventing them from understanding what data is expected.
findings.suggestion: Add aria-label attributes to these inputs or explicitly associate them with their visible text headers using standard <label for="..."> markup.
findings.source_hint: data-export.html (email, time range) and connected-apps.html (category, sort)

findings.user_goal: Review and revoke connected apps on a mobile device.
findings.problem: On mobile viewports, the connected app cards do not stack vertically. The side-by-side layout squashes the description text into a narrow column, and the 'Revoke' button collides with the bottom border of the card.
findings.evidence: Agent mobile observations: "connected app cards retain a side-by-side layout... forces the description text into a very narrow column with excessive wrapping" and "The 'Revoke' button on the mobile app cards lacks sufficient bottom padding".
findings.why_it_matters: The cramped layout makes the app descriptions difficult to read and makes the UI look broken and unpolished on small screens.
findings.suggestion: Update the mobile CSS (using media queries) to stack the app icon/title row and the description text vertically, and add proper margin/padding below the Revoke button.
findings.source_hint: connected-apps.html app cards on mobile viewports

gaps: Only directly exercised 59% of visible interactive feature signatures.
1 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
